correctness.rationale: For L2(0,1) and every integer n>=1, the integrated orthonormal Legendre recurrence exactly identifies E_n as a skew Jacobi tail. After phase rotation it is self-adjoint with b_(n,m)=2n/sqrt((2n+2m+1)(2n+2m+3)). The exact positive quadratic form and compact-embedding/tightness argument prove the Dirichlet Airy limit of its top edge, yielding |a_1|/2^(4/3) with the stated n^(5/3) normalization. The explicit Sturm--Liouville singular-value formula independently gives best same-rank error. The packaged checker replayed the Legendre coefficient identities for k=1..11 and eight finite Jacobi edge estimates; no finite computation is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Polynomial Galerkin compression of the indefinite-integration operator is a canonical finite-rank approximation used in spectral methods. The sharp operator-norm rate shows a universal pi/2 inefficiency relative to the optimal same-rank approximation, and the nonanalytic n^(-5/3) Airy correction quantitatively identifies a turning-point boundary layer not visible in smooth-input Galerkin estimates. The object and invariant are natural; the theorem is valid for every sufficiently large dimension rather than an arbitrary numerical instance.
